newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end lower in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end lower in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Lack of follow-up buying by speculators saw share prices drift lower at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, dealers said.
Market activity was generally dull, with attention focussed on select blue chips, they said.

"The market opened firm, but showed signs of weakness towards close on little buying support," said a dealer at an institutional brokerage. "Select bidding by foreign funds helped some stocks close with small gains."
The BSE's top 30-share index ended 17.50 points lower at a provisional 3,484.77 after rallying to 3,525.34 at mid-session.
Funds were bidders in blue chips such as Glaxo, Oriental Bank, Hindustan Petroleum, Indian Rayon, BSES and Hindalco, market sources said.

At the National Stock Exchange (NSE), tobacco conglomerate ITC was the top stock traded in volumes of over 14.67 million shares. The share jumped 12.50 rupees, or 3.07 percent, to end at 418.90, off the day's high of 426.50.

There was no single major factor behind the ITC price surge, dealers said. Bull operators were pushing up the stock, they added. ITC rose 8.0 rupees, or 1.95 percent, to 417.0 at the BSE with over 4.06 million shares traded.

"Foreign funds are looking at non-cyclicals -- telecoms, power, banks and a few auto firms that cater to the rural markets," Subra Subramanian, Indian research director at securities firm HG Asia, told Reuters.
Analysts said the low price-earnings ratios of Indian stocks, compared to other Asian markets, meant that there was a lot of potential for "good" price appreciations.
Among pivotal stocks, SBI lost 5.25 rupees to 277.50, Reliance 6.75 to 271.25, TISCO 4.25 to 194.50, L&T 3.50 to 244.0 and TELCO 2.25 to 331.0.
